title: Cheap AI Movies Are Riding the Coattails of Real Blockbusters
hook: As Christopher Nolan's big-budget Odyssey hit theaters, a fully AI-generated film with a nearly identical title quietly appeared online — the direct-to-video cash-grab playbook, remade with AI.
key_points: 'Odysseus: The Fall,' a fully AI-generated film from startup Fountain 0, released alongside Nolan's The Odyssey.
It was made on a 'mid-five-figures' budget, versus Nolan's roughly $250 million production.
AI-made films are filling the back catalogs of ad-supported streamers like Tubi, Roku Channel, and Amazon Freevee.
They trade name actors and original scripts for speed, scale, and search-friendly titles that piggyback on real releases.
A separate AI 'actor,' Tilly Norwood, set to star in an upcoming film, has drawn objections from the actors' union ACTRA.
content_html: Christopher Nolan's big-budget adaptation of The Odyssey drew crowds to theaters this year. Around the same time, a very differently made film with a nearly identical premise quietly showed up online: "Odysseus: The Fall," a fully AI-generated movie from startup Fountain 0, made on what The Verge describes as a "mid-five-figures" budget — a rounding error next to Nolan's roughly $250 million production.
extra_html: It's a modern spin on an old trick. Direct-to-video studios have always made cheap knockoffs timed to ride a real blockbuster's marketing, but generative AI makes that playbook dramatically faster and cheaper to run — hence the label "AI slop" for films built this way. These titles are increasingly filling the back catalogs of ad-supported streamers like Tubi, Roku Channel, and Amazon Freevee, trading recognizable actors and an original script for speed, scale, and a title designed to catch a confused search. The trend has a second front, too: an AI-generated "actor," Tilly Norwood, is set to headline an upcoming film, a move the actors' union ACTRA has objected to as a threat to human performers' livelihoods. None of this makes an AI film worthless on its own merits — but it's a good reason to actually check what you're pressing play on, especially when a title looks suspiciously familiar.

related.title: Can AI Be Creative?
related.hook: AI can write a poem or compose a tune that genuinely moves people. Whether that's 'real' creativity or very sophisticated remixing is a question with no settled answer — and it matters.

related.title: AI Images, Art & Video
related.hook: Type a sentence, get a picture. Image generators learned the link between words and visuals from billions of captioned images — which is also why artists are raising hard questions.
